what_happened: In slow highway traffic at about 3.5 m/s with a RIGHT command, the ego drifted left, about 2 m off the recorded path, onto the lane line and into the left lane. It sideswiped actor 51, which was travelling alongside in that lane (lateral collision).

In stop-and-go highway traffic, the ego kept closing on lead vehicle 5 in its own lane at about 3 m/s (reported gap 8.0→4.1 m) and hit its rear just 0.5 s after the policy took over at 4.7 s, while still exactly on the recorded human path (0.0 m off). Most of the closing happened during the log replay before handoff, so the policy had little time to brake, though it barely slowed (3.3→2.9 m/s); the ego was also rear-ended at some point.

In slow highway traffic, the ego was going straight in its lane and closing on lead vehicle 5 (gap shrinking from 8.0 m to 4.1 m) when its front touched 5's rear at 5.2 s. That was only 0.5 s after the policy took over at 4.7 s. In that time the policy slowed only slightly (3.3 to 2.9 m/s), and the ego stayed on the recorded human path (0.0 m off).

In slow highway traffic at about 3 m/s, the ego's front box touched lead vehicle 5 at 5.2 s, only 0.5 s after the policy took over. The ego was still exactly on the recorded human path (0.0 m off) and slowing slightly, so the contact most likely comes from the replayed lead's box or the actors' box sizes, not from a policy decision; the ego was also rear-ended at some point in the run.

The ego was replaying the recorded human drive, closing on the slower white utility truck ahead (actor 2) at about 5.6 m/s while the gap shrank from 12.6 m to 4.6 m. A front collision with that truck was flagged at 4.7 s, the same moment the policy took over, and the ego was still 0.0 m from the recording. So the contact comes from the logged trajectory and the actor's box overlap, not from anything the policy chose.

Before handoff, the ego was replaying the recorded trajectory (0.0 m off the recording) and gained speed from 4.2 to 5.6 m/s. Over that time the gap to the white utility truck ahead in its lane (actor 2) shrank from 12.6 m to 4.6 m, and the two boxes already overlap at 4.7 s. That is the same moment the policy took over, so the front collision was set up by the replay or by the actor's reconstructed position, and the policy had no time to react.

While replaying the recorded drive (0.0 m off the log), the ego closed from 12.6 m to 4.6 m on a white utility truck (actor 2) ahead in its lane. Their boxes overlap, which counts as a front collision, at 4.7 s, the same moment the policy took over, so the collision came from the replay, probably a mismatch in the truck's position or box size, and not from anything the policy did.
